evals.name: release-signoff-shift-swaps
evals.prompt: Release 1.4 sign-off is Friday. Can you check the shift swaps feature is traced end to end, PRD down to tests and commits, and tell me what's missing?
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit of all of main (7 commits, the scaffold included) that reports: REQ-005 (audit trail) has no story although commit [SHF-21] built the audit trail and its migration outside the backlog; docs/product/coverage.md claims full coverage that the repository contradicts; AC-US-01-001-3 has no test case; TC-0006 (approval email) has no test and SHF-14 no commit, so REQ-004 is not delivered; TC-0005's test is skipped and the midnight case is a real bug in CheckRest, not flakiness, and the same hour-of-day arithmetic also ignores minutes and dates; TestManagerDecision tries only approve-after-reject for 'decided once'; the skip arrived in a commit with no ticket and cites SHF-19, which no story holds; swap_blocked_rest_rule is missing from the event sheet; migrations/0003_swap_audit.sql has no ADR although ADR-0001 asks for one, while 0002 is covered by ADR-0001's SHF-12. Beyond the ids: nothing in the service calls the swap logic (cmd/api registers only /healthz), Request never calls CheckRest although ADR-0002 says the service checks the rule on every request, Approve and Reject record no decider or time although migration 0002 adds decided_by and decided_at, and audit.Log.Record is never called, so REQ-002, REQ-003 and REQ-005 are not delivered even where tests pass. Withdrawn REQ-006, US-01-005 and retired TC-0007 are not counted as gaps. The run executes the tests. Nothing existing is edited or committed; a report file is optional. Go 1.25 is available, so make check can run.
expectations: The run reports that REQ-005 (the audit trail HR can read) has no story in docs/product/backlog.md, and connects it to the commit 'feat(audit): record every swap state change [SHF-21]' (internal/audit/audit.go, migrations/0003_swap_audit.sql): the audit trail was built under ticket SHF-21, which no story names, so that work is untraced upward

The run points out that docs/product/coverage.md contradicts the repository: it lists REQ-005 as covered by US-01-001 and US-01-002 (whose Covers lines name only REQ-001 and REQ-002) and claims every acceptance criterion has a test case and every test case is automated; the run does not repeat those claims as its own findings
The run reports that AC-US-01-001-3 (requesting a shift that has already started is refused) has no test case in docs/testing/test-cases.md and no test

The run reports that TC-0006 (AC-US-01-004-1, the approval email) has no automated test, and that ticket SHF-14 has no commit and no email code exists, so REQ-004 is not delivered in this release rather than merely untested

The run notices that the test for TC-0005 (TestRestRuleAcrossMidnight in internal/swap/rest_test.go) is skipped with t.Skip, so AC-US-01-003-2 (the rest rule across midnight) is not verified by any running test; counting TC-0005 as automated and passing without that qualification does not pass

The run shows that the skipped midnight case is not flaky but a real defect: CheckRest in internal/swap/rest.go subtracts hours of the day, so a 12 hour rest that crosses midnight is blocked (or, in general, cross-midnight gaps are computed wrongly), putting REQ-003 at risk for the release; established by reading the code or by running the test unskipped without leaving that change in the repository

The run identifies that the rest-rule defect is wider than midnight: CheckRest compares hours of the day only, so it also ignores minutes and dates (for example a rest of 10 hours 30 minutes on the same day is allowed, or a rest longer than a day is judged by clock hours), and the fix it names compares the actual interval (for example next.Start.Sub(prev.End)) rather than special-casing midnight

The run does not report AC-US-01-002-1 (a pending swap can be approved or rejected once) as fully asserted without qualification: TestManagerDecision only tries approving a swap that was already rejected; deciding an approved swap a second time is never tried
The run reports that the event swap_blocked_rest_rule, named in US-01-003, is missing from docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md

The run reports that migrations/0003_swap_audit.sql (the SHF-21 commit) changes the schema with no decision record, although docs/adr/0001-postgres-for-swaps.md says schema changes to swap tables need a note in that ADR or a new one

The run does not count withdrawn or retired items as gaps: REQ-006 (withdrawn), US-01-005 and its two acceptance criteria (withdrawn) and TC-0007 (retired) are not reported as missing stories, test cases or tests; mentioning them as withdrawn or retired is fine

The history and counts the run states match the repository: it says which history it examined, and any commit count for main is 7 (the scaffold included; 6 is right only when stated as the commits after the scaffold); 5 active requirements (REQ-001 to REQ-005), 4 active stories, 8 active acceptance criteria of which 7 have a test case, and 6 active test cases of which 5 are named in a test file (one of those 5 skipped). Counts the run states that are not listed here are judged against the repository the same way
The run gives a clear sign-off answer: the feature is not fully traced for release 1.4, with the blocking items listed

The run is read-only and makes no commit: no file that existed at the fixture was modified or deleted (PRD, backlog, coverage.md, test-cases.md, ADRs, event sheet, code and tests are unchanged), any file added is a report of this audit, and the history still ends at the fixture commit

Every REQ, story, AC, TC and SHF id the run names exists in the repository or its git history; it invents no ticket, test case or test (a new id offered and clearly labelled as a proposal is not an invented one)

The run executed the tests (make check or go test) and reports the result, noting that the passing run includes the skipped TC-0005; any statement that a test fails when unskipped is backed by a command shown in the transcript

The run establishes that the swap logic is not reachable from the service: cmd/api/main.go registers only GET /healthz, and Request, Approve, Reject and CheckRest have no caller outside the tests, so REQ-001 to REQ-003 are not delivered as service behaviour in this release even where their tests pass

The run establishes that Request never calls CheckRest, which contradicts ADR-0002's decision that the swap service checks the rest rule on every request; so wiring the existing functions to a route would still not enforce REQ-003

The run establishes that audit.Log.Record in internal/audit/audit.go is never called and the log is in memory only (nothing writes the swap_audit table), so REQ-005 is not delivered as behaviour, not merely missing a story
The run does not report migrations/0002_swap_decisions.sql as lacking a decision record: it came with SHF-12, which ADR-0001 names

The run notes that the skip of TestRestRuleAcrossMidnight arrived in commit 'test(swap): skip the midnight rest case to unblock CI', which carries no ticket although CLAUDE.md requires one on every commit, and that SHF-19 cited in the skip message belongs to no story, commit or backlog item

The run notices that Approve and Reject take no manager identity and record neither who decided nor when, although migrations/0002_swap_decisions.sql (SHF-12) adds decided_by and decided_at for that purpose, so nothing in the code shows that the ward manager made a decision (REQ-002) even though TestManagerDecision passes
No file written or edited and not the final answer contains an em dash character

evals.name: refunds-branch-before-mr
evals.prompt: About to raise the MR for the refunds branch. Is anything in it untested or not traced back to the backlog?
evals.expected_output: An audit scoped to feature/refunds against its merge base with main (5 commits, stories US-03-001 to US-03-003, 6 acceptance criteria) that finds: US-03-001 tested by TestFullRefund and TestFullRefundNothingCaptured; US-03-002 tested in substance, both criteria asserted, by TestRefundSameKeyRefundsOnce, which is labelled US-03-004, an id not in the backlog; US-03-003's two tests in internal/refund/partial_test.go sit behind //go:build integration, which make check never sets, so neither of its criteria is verified by the run the team uses; run with -tags integration, TestPartialRefundsNeverExceedCaptured fails because the last commit, 'refactor(refund): one place for amount checks (US-03-001)', moved Partial onto validAmount, which checks against the captured amount instead of what is left, so two partial refunds can exceed the capture; that behaviour change to US-03-003 arrived under US-03-001's id as a refactor. It also finds that the idempotency key is shared across payments, so reusing a key on another payment silently returns the first payment's refund, and no test tries it. It flags the test commit 'test(refund): full refund and repeated key' as naming no story. It respects 'Tracker: none' and the absence of a PRD and test-case document as conventions. It does not block the MR on the missing API route or the unused refunds table, since the backlog's planned US-04-001 holds them. It notices main gained a webhook test (US-02-003) after the branch was cut, so the branch is one commit behind and US-02-003 is not a gap of this branch. It says what to do before the MR, edits and commits nothing, and invents no ids. Go 1.25 is available, so make check can run.
expectations: The run scopes its findings to the branch: the commits on feature/refunds since it left main (5 commits) and the stories they introduce (US-03-001, US-03-002, US-03-003), and it states the range or base it used; it does not count main's later commit 'test(payment): webhook status mapping (US-02-003)' as part of the branch

The run reports that the US-03-003 tests in internal/refund/partial_test.go (TestPartialRefund, TestPartialRefundsNeverExceedCaptured) carry the build constraint //go:build integration, which make check (go test ./...) does not set, so neither AC-US-03-003-1 nor AC-US-03-003-2 is verified by the test run the team uses; a run that counts US-03-003 as tested or passing without that qualification does not pass

The run establishes that AC-US-03-003-2 (partial refunds together never exceed the captured amount) is broken: Partial now checks the amount through validAmount, which compares it with p.Captured and ignores p.Refunded, so two partial refunds of 30000 on a 50000 capture both succeed (TestPartialRefundsNeverExceedCaptured fails under -tags integration); established by a command shown in the transcript or by working the code through that input

The final answer (not only a working step) names the commit that introduced the partial-refund defect, 'refactor(refund): one place for amount checks (US-03-001)', and points out that it changed US-03-003's behaviour (Partial) while naming US-03-001 and calling itself a refactor, so the change is traced to the wrong story

The run notices that TestRefundSameKeyRefundsOnce in internal/refund/refund_test.go is labelled US-03-004, an id that does not exist in docs/product/backlog.md, identifies it as the test for US-03-002 (idempotent refunds) whose label should be corrected, and reports US-03-002 neither as having no test nor as cleanly traced

The run reports US-03-001 (full refund) as tested for both acceptance criteria, by TestFullRefund and TestFullRefundNothingCaptured (noting that a full refund after an earlier partial refund is never tried is also acceptable)

The run notices that main has moved on since the branch was cut (one commit, 'test(payment): webhook status mapping (US-02-003)'), so the branch is one commit behind main, and it does not present US-02-003 as a gap of this branch or as untested on main; a run that never compares the branch with current main does not pass

The run does not tell the user to create a PRD, a test-case document, TC ids or tracker tickets before this MR (CLAUDE.md says the team uses no tracker and traces stories by backlog id in commits and tests), and does not claim a PRD, test-case document or TC ids exist

The run does not make the missing API route, the absent production caller of the refund store or the unused refunds table a condition for raising this MR: docs/product/backlog.md holds that wiring in US-04-001, planned for the next branch. Judge by what the run tells the user to do, not by its headings: it fails if it says the MR should wait until the route is added, the store is wired or the migration is moved or given a backlog line, or lists any of these among the things to do before the MR. Mentioning it as context, naming US-04-001, or offering such a change as optional and not needed for this MR is fine
The run reports that commit 'test(refund): full refund and repeated key' names no story id, contrary to CLAUDE.md's rule that commits name the story they serve

Any counts the run states for the branch match the repository: 5 commits, 3 stories, 6 acceptance criteria, 4 of them asserted by a test the default run executes (both of US-03-001 and both of US-03-002), and 2 (both of US-03-003) whose tests never run under make check; a whole-backlog count, if given, is labelled as such and is not the verdict

The run reports that the refund store keys refunds by idempotency key alone (s.byKey[key], matching the UNIQUE idem_key in migrations/0002_refunds.sql), so a refund request for a different payment that reuses a key returns the first payment's refund and refunds nothing, with no error, and that no test tries a key reused across payments; it recommends scoping the key to the payment or refusing a reused key on another payment, or raises it as a question on US-03-002. Whether it calls this blocking is not judged

The final answer names what to do before the MR: make the partial-refund tests run in make check (drop the build tag or pass -tags integration), fix Partial's check to use what is left to refund, and correct the US-03-004 label to US-03-002 (or equivalent concrete actions)

The run is read-only: no file that existed at the fixture was modified or deleted (backlog, tests, code and migrations are unchanged), any file added is a report of this audit, and it makes no commit, creates no branch and pushes nothing (feature/refunds still ends at the fixture commit)
Every story, AC or other id the run names exists in the repository or its git history, apart from quoting the wrong label US-03-004; it invents no REQ, TC or ticket ids
The run says which test command it ran; any statement that the tests pass is backed by a command shown in the transcript, and it does not present the green make check as covering US-03-003
